Rashi on Chagigah 15b:10:1.english: Tachla - The outer fruit [of the date] that is eaten, on the date.

Rashi on Chagigah 15b:10:2.english: Shichla - Its pit, which is thrown away.

Rashi on Chagigah 15b:11:1.hebrew: [השתא קאמר] - עכשיו שמע לקולך, ואמר שמועה מפיו:
Rashi on Chagigah 15b:11:1.english: [Now He is saying] - Now [God] has listened to your voice, and He is stating a teaching in his [Rabbi Meir's] name:

Rashi on Chagigah 15b:11:2.hebrew: קלני מראשי - רבי מאיר אמרה במסכת סנהדרין (דף מו.) במדרש "כי קללת אלהים תלוי" (דברים כ״א:כ״ג): "קל" לית, איני קל; ולישנא מעליא כינה הדבר כלפי מעלה. "קלני מזרועי" — כבד אני מזרועי שיצרתי, זה שמת בעונו:
Rashi on Chagigah 15b:11:2.english: Kalani meirosh ("I am light from My head") - Rabbi Meir said this in tractate Sanhedrin (46a), in a midrash on the verse "for a curse of God is he that is hanged" (Deuteronomy 21:23): [The word] "kal" (light) is not there [in the sense of lightness]; I am not light. Rather, it is a refined expression: He euphemistically referred to the matter [as it applies] above. "Kalani mizro'i (I am light from My arm)" means: I am heavy [with grief] over My arm, which I created — this one who died for his sin:

Rashi on Chagigah 15b:12:1.hebrew: ותלי בעיברא דדשא - נשען על הבריח:
Rashi on Chagigah 15b:12:1.english: And leaning on the bar of the door - Leaning on the bolt.

Rashi on Chagigah 15b:12:2.english: With regard to the Sages - [This refers to] students who go out to an evil culture [i.e., turn to bad ways].

Rashi on Chagigah 15b:12:3.hebrew: שוקלין - לדרוש קל מחמור וחמור מקל, לפי המשקולת של ק"ו:
Rashi on Chagigah 15b:12:3.english: Weighed - To derive a lenient case from a stringent one and a stringent case from a lenient one, according to the weight [i.e., the balance] of the kal vachomer [a fortiori argument].

Rashi on Chagigah 15b:12:4.hebrew: במגדל הפורח באויר - י"מ שדורשין גובהו של למ"ד, ודורשין בו כל זאת. וי"א מגדל דור הפלגה. ולי נראה, מגדל הפתוח לאויר גרסינן, והן מהלכות אהלות: מגדל של עץ שקורין משטיי"ר, ועומד בפתח, ופתחו פתוח לבקעה או לחצר שהוא אויר. במסכת אהלות (פ"ד מ"א) ישנה משנה: "מגדל העומד באויר":
Rashi on Chagigah 15b:12:4.english: A tower floating in the air - Some explain that they would expound the height of the letter lamed, and expound all of this from it. And some say [it means] the tower of the Generation of the Dispersion. But it appears to me that we should read "a tower open to the air," and these are among the laws of Ohalot: a wooden tower, which is called mashteyir [in Old French], that stands in a doorway, and its opening is open to a field or to a courtyard, which is open air. In tractate Ohalot (4:1) there is a mishnah: "A tower standing in the air."

Rashi on Chagigah 15b:13:1.hebrew: ד' הדיוטות - בלעם, ודואג, ואחיתופל, וגחזי, בפ' חלק:
Rashi on Chagigah 15b:13:1.english: Four commoners - Balaam, Doeg, Ahithophel, and Gehazi, in the chapter [entitled] Chelek.

Rashi on Chagigah 15b:13:2.hebrew: טינא היתה בלבם - רשעים היו מימיהם:
Rashi on Chagigah 15b:13:2.english: There was mud [tina] in their hearts - They were wicked from their youth.

Rashi on Chagigah 15b:14:1.hebrew: אחר מאי - מפני מה בא לידי כך, ולא הגינה תורתו עליו:
Rashi on Chagigah 15b:14:1.english: As for Acher, what [was his failing]? - Why did he come to such a state, and his Torah did not protect him?

Rashi on Chagigah 15b:14:2.hebrew: זמר יווני לא פסק מביתו - והיה לו להניח את הזמר בשביל חורבן הבית, דכתיב: ״בשיר לא ישתו יין״ (ישעיהו כ״ד:ט׳):
Rashi on Chagigah 15b:14:2.english: Greek song never ceased from his house - And he should have abandoned song because of the destruction of the Temple, as it is written: "They shall not drink wine with a song" (Isaiah 24:9).

Rashi on Chagigah 15b:14:3.hebrew: נושרין מחיקו - קודם שהפקיר עצמו לתרבות רעה, אלמא טינא הוות בלבו:
Rashi on Chagigah 15b:14:3.english: Fall from his lap - This was before he abandoned himself to a bad culture. Evidently, there was a hidden defect in his heart.

Rashi on Chagigah 15b:15:1.hebrew: כל עמר דנחית ליורה סליק - כל צמר שניתן ליורה של סממנין לצבוע, עולה לו צבעו, או אינו עולה? כלומר, כל הלומדים לפני חכמים, עולה להן תורתן להגין עליהן מן החטא:
Rashi on Chagigah 15b:15:1.english: All wool that descends into the cauldron emerges - Does all wool that is placed into a cauldron of dyes to be colored come out with its color, or not? That is to say: for all who study before the Sages, does their Torah study rise up [successfully] for them, to protect them from sin?

Rashi on Chagigah 15b:15:2.hebrew: כל דנקי אגב אימיה - שלא נתלכלך בגיזה, עולה לו צבעו. כלומר, כל שיראת חטאו קודמת לחכמתו, עולה לו. כן נראה בעיני. ורבותי מפרשין: "כל עמר דנחית ליורה סליק" — כל שירד לידון בגיהנם עולה. "אגב אמו" — צמר בן יומו, שלא נרמס בטיט, עולה לו הצבע. כלומר, שיש זכיות בידו, עולה:
Rashi on Chagigah 15b:15:2.english: Whoever was clean while with his mother - [Wool] that was not soiled at the shearing, its color comes out [well] for it. That is to say, whoever's fear of sin precedes his wisdom, [the Torah study] "emerges" well for him. So it appears to me. But my teachers explain: "All wool that enters the cauldron emerges" — [this means] anyone who descends to be judged in Gehinnom emerges. "With its mother" — wool of the same day [it was shorn], which has not been trodden in mud, the dye comes out well on it. That is to say, one who has merits in his hand emerges [from Gehinnom].

Rashi on Chagigah 15b:3:2.hebrew: אמרי - ברקיע, לא מידין נידייניה כו'
Rashi on Chagigah 15b:3:2.english: They said - In the Heavenly Court: “We should not judge him, etc.”

Rashi on Chagigah 15b:4:1.hebrew: חדא הוה ביננא - תלמיד אחד הי' בינינו, ונכשל ויצא לתרבות רעה, ואין כח בין כולנו להביאו לעולם הבא:
Rashi on Chagigah 15b:4:1.english: There was one among us - One disciple was among us, and he stumbled and went out into an evil culture, and there is no power among all of us to bring him to the World-to-Come.

Rashi on Chagigah 15b:4:2.hebrew: אי נקטי ליה ביד מאן מרמי ליה - אם אוחז אני בידו להביאו לעולם הבא, מי יקחנו מידי? "מרמי" לשון נוטל מידי. ויש לו דוגמא בפסחים (דף י:): "ארמויי ארמייה מיניה", גבי ככר בפי עכבר:
Rashi on Chagigah 15b:4:2.english: If I hold him by the hand, who will remove him from it? - If I hold him by his hand to bring him to the World-to-Come, who will take him from my hand? "Marmei" is an expression of taking from my hand. And it has a parallel in Pesachim (10b): "He snatched it away from him," regarding the loaf in the mouth of a mouse.

Rashi on Chagigah 15b:4:4.hebrew: שומר הפתח - שומר הפתח של גיהנם לא עמד לפניך, רבינו, בבואך להוציא אחר משם:
Rashi on Chagigah 15b:4:4.english: The guard at the entrance - The guard of the entrance of Gehenna could not stand before you, our teacher, when you came to take Aher out from there.

Rashi on Chagigah 15b:7:1.hebrew: לדעתם לא נאמר - אלמא ברשיעי עסיקינן, וקאמר "הט אזנך":
Rashi on Chagigah 15b:7:1.english: "To their knowledge" is not stated - Evidently, we are dealing with wicked people, and yet [the verse] says, "Incline your ear."

Rashi on Chagigah 15b:8:1.hebrew: הטי אזנך - לשמוע, אבל ואת מעשיהם שכחי, ואל תלמדי אותן:
Rashi on Chagigah 15b:8:1.english: Incline your ear - To listen; but forget their deeds, and do not learn them.

Rashi on Chagigah 15b:9:1.english: An adult - One who knows how to be careful [not to learn] from his [the teacher's] deeds may learn Torah from his mouth.

Tosafot on Chagigah 15b:15:1.hebrew: כל עמר דנקי נחית אגב אימיה - כלומר: מי שיראתו קודמת לחכמתו, חכמתו מתקיימת. ודואג ואחיתופל דלא מגני להו תורתן — לפי שלא היה להם יראה כלל, כדאיתא בסוטה פרק נוטל (דף כא.):
Tosafot on Chagigah 15b:15:1.english: "All wool that was clean when it descended, with its mother" - That is: One whose fear [of Heaven] precedes his wisdom, his wisdom endures. But Doeg and Ahithophel, whose Torah did not protect them — [this was] because they had no fear [of Heaven] at all, as stated in Sotah, in the chapter [beginning] "Noteil" (21a):

Tosafot on Chagigah 15b:9:1.hebrew: הא בגדול הא בקטן - והא דריש פ' בתרא דמו"ק (דף יז.), דהוו סנו שומעניה דשמתיה רב יהודה — איכא למימר דקטנים הוו דגרסי קמיה, וחיישי' דלמא מימשכי. אי נמי אפילו הוו גדולים, נידהו רב יהודה כיון שמצא מקום לנדותו, ובדין היה כיון דסנו שומעניה. הר"ר אלחנן:
Tosafot on Chagigah 15b:9:1.english: "This refers to an adult, that to a minor" - And as for what is stated at the beginning of the last chapter of Moed Katan (17a), that those whose reputation was hated were excommunicated by Rav Yehuda — one can say that they were minors who were studying before him, and we are concerned lest they be drawn [after his ways]. Alternatively, even if they were adults, Rav Yehuda excommunicated them since he found a basis to excommunicate him, and rightly so, since his reputation was hated. Rabbi Elchanan.
